title: Immunizations
before:
Immunizations remain the single most effective way to protect against many diseases and some cancers. The immunization schedule is designed to provide immunity (protection) early in life before children are likely to be exposed to serious, potentially life-threatening diseases. Vaccines are safe and effective at preventing serious diseases. Maine law requires children to be vaccinated against certain diseases before they can attend any public or private school in the state. Keeping children healthy in a group setting is essential. These requirements help protect all children, including those who cannot be vaccinated for medical reasons, by reducing the spread of infectious disease. 

Immunization Resources
  • State of Maine Immunization Requirements for Maine Schools (updated 5/25/2026)
  • Maine Centers for Disease Control & Prevention: Immunization Resources for School Nurses
  • Maine School Vaccine Requirements Reference Guide
  • School Immunization Rule FAQ Updated July 2026
  • Sample Forms & Templates
  • Annual Vaccine Provider Training - The Maine Immunization Program requires that all enrolled providers complete the Vaccines For Children Training on an annual basis. This is required for both the primary and secondary vaccine coordinators.

A Medical exemption is to be provided by the parent/student and must be a written statement from a Maine licensed physician, nurse practitioner, or physician assistant that, in the licensed physician's, nurse practitioner's, or physician assistant's professional judgment, immunization against one or more of the diseases may be medically inadvisable.

The Docket for Schools (DFS) platform went live September 2025. This new tool is designed to support school nurses in identifying immunization gaps and ensuring uniform compliance with Maine school vaccination laws. All Maine public and private schools are required to report the immunization status of students through DFS. 

  • Docket for Schools Resource Library

School Nurses may also access student immunization records by accessing Maine's statewide immunization registry. 

  • Maine Immunization Information System (ImmPact) 

For more information, please reach out to the ImmPact Help Desk at either 207-287-3006 or Immpact.Support@Maine.gov

2026-2027 School-Located Vaccine Clinic Toolkit

The Maine Department of Education and the Maine Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Maine CDC) support Maine schools and community health partner's efforts to provide school-located vaccines if they choose to do so. The past efforts of school nurses and community health partners have led to improved health and attendance of school-aged children. 

  • Maine Immunization Program (Maine CDC) Provider Portal & Resources
Please visit the Maine Center for Disease Control & Prevention for the most up-to-date information regarding Influenza at MaineFlu.gov. 

Contact

notes: 422 words with no section headers at all — the biggest single improvement available here.

decisions.label: Jumbotron callouts become notes
decisions.why: 1 callout is built as a Bootstrap jumbotron, which the component list replaced with dc-note and which Bootstrap itself removed in version 5. Same content, the site's own callout.

decisions.label: Drop the dash once the link is set apart
decisions.why: 1 of those items separate the link from its description with a dash. The link is now set in the display face at a larger size with a chevron after it, so the dash marks a boundary that is already unmistakable. Only the separator is removed — no word changes.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 1 list item opens with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Make a loose address look like an address
decisions.why: 1 email address sits in the body of this page rather than in a contact block, drawn exactly like every other link — so the one that opens a mail window looks the same as the ones that go to web pages. The chip carries the same envelope the banner's contact link uses. The address itself does not change.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
